reason: The Book of Ruth portrays all virtuous characters positively regardless of social status. Ruth, a foreigner and common laborer, is explicitly described as an 'eshet chayil' (אשת חיל - a woman of excellence/valor). Naomi is presented as wise and faithful. Boaz, though a man of substance and influence, shows the same virtues of kindness and righteousness. The narrative emphasizes faithfulness, lovingkindness (chesed), and divine providence working through honorable actions by people at all levels. There is no moral conflict portraying common people as wrong and leaders as right; rather, the story celebrates virtue and proper conduct (including adherence to legal redemption procedures) across all characters, making it fundamentally about redemption, loyalty, and God's providential care rather than about social conflict between classes.
